title: Where Do We Go from Here?
coreMove: Redesign environments so practice, coaching, opportunity, and standards are built into the system rather than left to private luck.
sourcePressure: The closing chapter argues that education, workplaces, and institutions should change if human performance is more trainable than static talent stories suggest, with concrete standards and support structures. Frozen sidecar for chapter 9 contains no traceable named figure, study, place, date, or artifact beyond the authors and chapter mechanism; sourceAnchors stays empty rather than inventing one.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version becomes generic optimism about human potential or lowers standards in the name of access.

hook: principal with stopwatch and pep poster from old Peak draft
tryThisNow: think about how society should change

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: municipal lifeguard certification program redesigned for repeat practice
exampleSpecs.audience: a recreation director who wants safer guards without lowering the test
exampleSpecs.stakes: a one-day pass-fail course misses weak rescue skills until a real swimmer needs help
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Anna keeps the final standard, adds weekly timed rescue reps, trains feedback leads, and opens extra pool slots for candidates without private swim-club access
exampleSpecs.firstImage: rescue tubes lined along a wet tile edge before dawn

exampleSpecs.audience: a plant manager replacing sink-or-swim training with visible standards
exampleSpecs.stakes: scrap and injuries rise when novices learn only by being rushed into production
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: At 9:05 a.m., Jack moves one machine setup off the live line, installs a practice jig, and requires trained peer feedback before apprentices return to production
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a practice jig bolted to a scratched steel bench

exampleSpecs.domain: public library digital-skills lab for job seekers
exampleSpecs.audience: a program lead designing access plus standards
exampleSpecs.stakes: people without home computers are judged as low skill before they get practice conditions
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Nicolas turns open computer time into short resume-upload reps with a visible checklist, volunteer feedback, and repeat slots for anyone who misses the first attempt
exampleSpecs.firstImage: laminated upload checklists stacked beside public keyboard covers

exampleSpecs.audience: a training director who wants learning without blame theater
exampleSpecs.stakes: cases get discussed as shame or paperwork instead of becoming practice targets
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Astrid separates system review from one trainable clinical judgment, assigns simulation reps, and tracks whether the corrected cue appears in the next rotation
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a case timeline projected beside a covered simulation mannequin

exampleSpecs.domain: regional journalism fellowship for rural reporters
exampleSpecs.audience: an editor building coaching where talent pipelines used to be thin
exampleSpecs.stakes: promising reporters leave after being judged on final copy without editing practice
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Pablo predicts another fellowship will fail if it only assigns stories, then adds line-edit drills, beat memos, and editor calls before publication deadlines
exampleSpecs.firstImage: marked proofs clipped beside a rural county beat map

exampleSpecs.domain: city youth orchestra audition-prep access program
exampleSpecs.audience: an arts administrator balancing high standards with fair preparation
exampleSpecs.stakes: auditions reward private lessons unless public prep builds the missing practice environment
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You watch Hiroshi keep the audition excerpt unchanged, publish the rubric, provide coached mock auditions, and measure who improves after feedback
exampleSpecs.firstImage: audition excerpts clipped to black music stands in an empty hall

skillTargets: design institutions around practice not labels
keep standards while widening access to preparation
distinguish support structures from generic encouragement
evaluate whether a system creates feedback and opportunity

tryThisNowSpec: Look at one group you influence. Identify the current final test, then name one protected practice rep, one feedback giver, and one access barrier you could change before that test.
